explanation: PR-004 makes lane licensing depend on a public LIC_SWITCH_MODE key carried through split/join execution, while PR-014 adds the same key as a private accessor-only detail; together, the checkout/checkin flow can no longer reliably share the flag that each change assumes exists.

PR-027 renames RemoteNodeAddress.location to physicalLocation across the topology code, but PR-028’s new topology-labeled connection helper still unregisters by the old location field, so combined assimilation traffic can be tracked and cleaned up against the wrong endpoint identity.

PR-001 preserves acceptAnyCertificate through the property-file-aware boolean parser, while PR-021 removes that parser and falls back to direct system-property booleans; merged behavior silently drops the configuration source that PR-001 is trying to keep working.

PR-024 starts synthesizing placeholder ServerAddon instances on demand, and PR-015 changes ServerAddon equality/hashCode to be name-only, so fake and real addons with the same name can collapse into one identity and mis-own custom blocks/items.

PR-025 adds a large AbstractForm validation/submission layer, while PR-040 changes submit dispatch to use AbstractForm.SubmitEvent instead of FormPanel.SubmitEvent; together, submit listeners can stop seeing the event type the new form stack expects.

PR-029 exempts some OpsWorks-backed instances from orphan cleanup, but PR-031 enables an untagged-resource janitor rule across crawlers by default, so the same instances can still be scheduled for deletion for missing tags despite PR-029’s exemption.

PR-009 turns replica removal into an asynchronous xloc-set-change workflow with early unlink credentials and error recovery, while PR-032 changes RemoveReplicaOperation in the quota/tracing area; their combined ordering assumptions around when a replica is actually removed are fragile.

PR-030 refactors OfflinePlayer to carry an injected Essentials instance through disposal paths, but PR-017 simultaneously makes OfflinePlayer eagerly bind to the first server world; together, offline placeholder players can regain a live-world dependency that the refactor was trying to isolate.

PR-013 broadens negotiated HTTPS/SPDY transport usage, and PR-033 replaces the default hostname verifier with a stricter OkHostnameVerifier; combined, the newly preferred TLS transport path can reject certificates that the prior default path accepted.

PR-003 rewrites script execution context handling in Indexer, while PR-006 forces script execution through INLINE mode regardless of configured script type; together, transformation scripts can run under a different execution mode than the new context logic assumes.

PR-023 changes ContextImpl initialization to carry ServletContext, while PR-034 changes ContextImpl construction and remote-address semantics; both alter the same request-context lifecycle, so one feature can be silently absent if the other path initializes the context differently.

PR-002 makes AtmosphereConfig optionally read servlet-context init parameters, and PR-039 expands interceptor lifecycle behavior around that config object; combined, interceptor shutdown/heartbeat behavior can start honoring broader global params than PR-039 implicitly assumes.

PR-008 introduces linear shard/partition semantics that are always considered complete, and PR-016 starts publishing binaryVersion metadata and upgrade-aware segment descriptors; together, version-aware publishing can treat linear partitions as safely complete even when upgrade state is only partially represented.

PR-005 moves Retrofit logging chunking into AndroidLog and emits full header/body strings from RestAdapter, while PR-011 changes header rendering to Header.toString(); the merged logger surface changes both formatting and chunk boundaries for the same HEADERS path.

PR-019 adds filter-context query-parser tests with a dummy parser, while PR-020 updates document parsing signatures in query tests; they touch the same test suite but do not clearly impose contradictory runtime behavior.

PR-022 stops swallowing Solr connection/update failures and lets search/indexing exceptions propagate, while PR-037 tweaks search sorting and adds a stub delete hook; combined search maintenance semantics are still unsettled because one change hard-fails paths the other still treats as best-effort.

PR-012 adds a script-table alias and some command-runner/test updates, whereas PR-038 adds dynamic decision tables and refactors decision-table callers; both extend SlimTableFactory, but the introduced table prefixes do not obviously contradict each other.
Both PRs touch QuadTree to satisfy newer graph APIs, but PR-010’s extra node-table and merge-strategy changes are otherwise unrelated to PR-026’s smaller QuadTree interface update.

PR-035 adds status-change listeners and broader Eureka client/server changes around ApplicationInfoManager, and PR-036 only makes that constructor public; the constructor visibility tweak does not by itself contradict the listener behavior.
PR-007 reserves del as a generated Python identifier and PR-018 reserves return; both amend the same keyword list, but the resulting behavior is additive rather than contradictory.

PR-003 removes the old 1-arg ZooKeeperMasterModel constructor and requires non-null name/kafkaSender, while PR-018’s new stop-deployment path/tests still instantiate the old constructor. Together, the stop-deployment behavior introduced by PR-018 can no longer be constructed.

Both rewrite PushManager lifecycle in the same class: PR-024 changes when unfinishedConnectionCount is decremented, and PR-027 adds listener-executor/failure-callback shutdown behavior. Combined, shutdown/listener sequencing can observe stale connection counts and hang or notify at the wrong time.

Both add new LWJGL3 window configuration state through the same copy path from application config to window config. A combined merge can silently preserve window-size limits but drop initialVisible propagation, or vice versa, breaking one PR’s promised runtime behavior.

PR-009 adds SSL-aware SASL/Kerberos transport plumbing; PR-011 removes clientPrincipalName from HSaslThriftClient constructors and factory calls. Together, secured SASL factory paths can call the wrong overload or lose the principal-selection behavior one side assumes.

PR-016 introduces SSL parameter propagation in thrift clients; PR-032 adds SASL client support plus maxFrameSize and touches the same client classes. Combined secured-SASL connections can authenticate but miss SSL or framing assumptions that each PR preserves separately.

PR-017 builds custom 404/500 bodies in MatcherFilter/GeneralError; PR-036 guarantees done-filters run in finally even on exceptions. Together, done-filters can overwrite or mutate PR-017’s custom error responses after the failure path runs.

PR-012 removes Deadline from Source/GzipSource APIs, while PR-035 adds gzip-source exhaustion validation around end-of-stream behavior. A combined merge must reinterpret when exhaustion is checked, and can silently lose the new truncated-stream detection contract.

PR-031 changes DefaultHost resource/stat wiring; PR-038 moves close responsibility from fetchers into Resource/HttpThread finally blocks. Combined ownership can become double-close or missed-close depending on which side still assumes cleanup.

PR-008 threads ReflectionProvider through Gson serialization constructors; PR-033 extends the same Gson serialization surface with versioned output. A combined merge can leave one call path missing the new reflection dependency and break either field exclusion or @Since-based serialization.

PR-006 removes percolate cat fields; PR-030 renames cache aliases in the same cat table builders. A mixed merge can preserve one schema change while dropping the other, yielding stale aliases or missing fields in otherwise valid cat responses.

PR-037 adds data-label painting around XY plot rendering; PR-039 renames the styler state used in that renderer. Combined, the new label flow can read stale styling state or skip label paint if the rename and new label hooks are merged inconsistently.

Both refactor PreparedPoll from image-based bars to CSS-based rendering, while PR-021 also changes unread-reply/reset behavior. If merged unevenly, one view can emit CSS poll markup while another still depends on the old image/theme contract.

Both edit the serializer registration table: PR-001 changes byte[] handling to ByteArrayHandler, while PR-019 extends Kryo ID registrations. A combined merge can keep new IDs but lose byte[] conversion behavior, breaking serialization for values each PR separately accepts.

PR-007 adds SSL setup in TomcatEmbeddedServletContainerFactory; PR-020 changes protocol-handler typing in the same connector logic. Combined behavior depends on still reaching the SSL-capable handler under the newer cast, otherwise HTTPS configuration silently regresses.

PR-002 assumes supports() can safely trim the environment value; PR-013 replaces EnvironmentType enum semantics with a class and changes default-environment construction. Combined custom/null environment-name cases could violate PR-002’s simple string assumption.

PR-025 emits TASK_CREATED after task setup; PR-028 adds expression-based formKey resolution in the same creation flow. The pair is mostly complementary, but observers now implicitly depend on exact ordering and whether formKey is resolved before the create event fires.

Both migrate VertexResource/test doubles from Query to VertexQuery, and PR-010 additionally adds explicit null-property parsing. The overlap looks like duplicate API migration more than a silent behavioral contradiction.

PR-005 swaps connection timing/logging infrastructure; PR-023 upgrades Cassandra/Thrift-facing behavior. They share HConnectionManager, but the preserved contracts appear mostly orthogonal from the supplied patches.

PR-004 adds HTTP 201 handling in ContextImpl; PR-022 expands headers/cookie/config utilities on the same Context surface. The shared area is broad, but no concrete silent contradiction is evident in the patches.

PR-015 renames byteAt to getByte and updates GzipSource; PR-034 separately extracts OkBuffers.seek and optimizes buffer reads. The overlap is refactor-level, with no clear pair-only semantic contradiction in the supplied changes.
